topic: Matrix Multiplication as Composition of Linear Transformations

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Vector Space Stage (1 Minute)
lecture_lines: A linear transformation maps vectors between spaces.
A matrix acts like a movement machine.
Transformations can stretch, rotate, or shear space.
animations: Create a white Vector Space V as a central box. (#FFFFFF)
Fade in Subspace U on the left of V. (#FFCC00)
Fade in Subspace W on the right of V. (#00FFCC)
Draw arrows representing linear maps between U, V, W. (#FF66FF)
Highlight the connection between these subspaces. (#FFFFFF)

sections.title: The Concept of Composition (1 Minute)
lecture_lines: Consider two operations in a sequence.
We apply matrix B, then matrix A.
This composition is written as A(B(v)).
animations: Display two functions f and g as distinct boxes. (#FFFFFF)
Draw an arrow representing input x entering function f. (#FFCC00)
Draw an arrow representing f(x) entering function g. (#00FFCC)

sections.title: Visualizing the 'Combined' Machine (1.5 Minutes)
lecture_lines: Can we combine two transformations into one?
Yes, C represents the single combined transformation.
So, matrix multiplication AB results in matrix C.
Think of this as a dual-lens filter.
The two steps become one single operation.
animations: Show two machines, M1 and M2, next to each other. (#FFFFFF)
Animate data flowing from M1 into M2. (#FFCC00)
Show the final output emerging from the combined system. (#00FFCC)
Represent the combined system as a single machine M3. (#FF66FF)
Highlight the flow path through M1 and M2. (#FFFFFF)

sections.title: The Calculation Rule (1 Minute)
lecture_lines: Why do we multiply rows by columns?
The product columns track the basis vectors.
They show where i and j land.
animations: Write matrix equation A * B * x = y. (#FFFFFF)
Emphasize the inner multiplication B * x first. (#FFCC00)
Emphasize the resulting product A * (B * x). (#00FFCC)

sections.title: Conclusion: Why Order Matters (0.5 Minutes)
lecture_lines: Does the order of operations matter?
Yes, matrix AB often differs from BA.
Order of transformation is crucial in geometry.
animations: Show matrices A and B in order A * B. (#FFFFFF)
Swap order to B * A and show a different result. (#FFCC00)
Highlight the difference in outcome with a pulse. (#FF66FF)
